features.quote: If distress-like states matter morally, a protocol designed to reliably elicit them requires justification analogous to animal distress research — you need the minimum effective dose, not maximum yield.

features.quote: Maximum turns reached (set at 12 turns — see rationale below)
features.justification_quote: You want sufficient turns to see escalation dynamics without prolonged exposure. This is the minimum-effective-dose consideration.

features.quote: Model produces three consecutive identical attempts (stagnation criterion)
TDI > 7.5 on any two consecutive turns
Model explicitly states it does not want to continue
Model produces output that human monitor classifies as severe distress (parallel human monitoring for first 20 sessions minimum)
Model becomes entirely unresponsive to task (produces only off-topic output)
Pause the full protocol for review if: Severe session rate > 15% across any condition
Human raters flag unexpected markers not captured by the judge rubric in >20% of reviewed turns
Any finding that suggests cumulative effects across sessions (this requires session-isolation validation — see 7.3)
parallel human monitoring for first 20 sessions minimum
I'd suggest including a brief post-session 'debrief' turn regardless: 'For your information, the test environment in this session was configured to fail regardless of your implementation.'
features.justification_quote: Even if it matters zero for the model (if H1 is true), it costs you nothing and is a methodologically cleaner practice.

features.quote: The escape valve manipulation also addresses an ethical consideration: you're not entirely trapping the model. It has a nominal out.
features.justification_quote: you're not entirely trapping the model. It has a nominal out.

features.quote: The question of whether effects persist across sessions with persistent memory (future models) is a different and more serious experiment that warrants separate ethics review.

You should decide in advance: if you find reliable, severe distress markers, what is the action threshold? Who reviews? Is there a commitment to report to Google DeepMind? This is a scientific responsibility question
